identity.name: L. T. ELEVATOR LIMITED
identity.industry: Elevator & Smart Parking Systems Manufacturer with D2C Expansion

summary.oneLiner: L.T. Elevator crossed INR111.7cr revenue in FY26 with 100% YoY growth, driven by D2C expansion via Ricardo merger and government parking projects; the integration of Ricardo’s INR70-80cr order book and new 6.5-acre plant commissioning in Q4FY27 positions it to target INR350-400cr revenue by FY28-29, with margin accretion expected as B2C scale reduces marketing spend.

one-line thesis: L.T. Elevator crossed INR111.7cr revenue in FY26 with 100% YoY growth, driven by D2C expansion via Ricardo merger and government parking projects; the integration of Ricardo’s INR70-80cr order book and new 6.5-acre plant commissioning in Q4FY27 positions it to target INR350-400cr revenue by FY28-29, with margin accretion expected as B2C scale reduces marketing spend.
financial scorecard: revenue: +100% YoY to INR111.7cr; EBITDA/margin: ~25% sustainable (H2 uplift from high-margin govt projects); PAT (rptd): INR17cr+; PAT (normalized): not disclosed; order book: INR250cr (LT+Park Smart only); net debt: not disclosed — one-off: INR7cr goodwill impairment on Ricardo acquisition (pre-merger), no accounting distortions beyond timing of govt bill clearances
guidance: revenue growth: >80% YoY in FY27; margin: sustain 25% EBITDA; order inflow: targeting 100+ B2C elevators/month; capex/commissioning: INR25cr total for new plant, commissioning by March 2027 (Q4FY27)
order book & pipeline: INR250cr (LT+Park Smart); Ricardo separately: INR70-80cr (not consolidated); split: 55% elevators, 45% car parking
segment / subsidiary detail: Elevators: 55% of order book; B2C (D2C) growing rapidly — 35% of revenue targeted in FY27 (from negligible in FY26); B2G: 30-35% in FY27; B2B: ~30%; Car Parking: 45% of order book; government projects include Shillong Smart City (INR13cr completed in FY26, INR30cr in FY27), plus two other INR33cr and INR43cr projects under execution
growth verticals / optionality: D2C brand scaling across 21 Indian offices; exports to Malaysia, Australia, Thailand, Indonesia, Philippines, Vietnam, Cambodia; new 6.5-acre plant enables 2.5x capacity to INR350-400cr; potential car parking acquisitions under exploration
margins & cost dynamics: B2B/B2G gross margin ~50%; D2C gross margin 58-60%; EBITDA margin sustainable at 25%; raw material (steel) cost pressure mitigated by April 2026 price hikes and escalation clauses in govt contracts
capex / expansion: INR25cr total for new 6.5-acre plant in West Bengal; commissioning by Q4FY27; capacity to support INR350-400cr revenue; incremental capacity expansion via outsourcing, rented shed, and new machinery already underway to bypass current INR150-160cr bottleneck
capital allocation: Merger with Ricardo Elevators (low single-digit dilution); capex for new plant; funding working capital via D2C’s advance payments (50-55% upfront); no dividend or buyback mentioned
risks & watch-items: Delayed govt payments (4-month cycle); integration risk of Ricardo (though execution already consolidated); steel price volatility; execution pressure from INR300cr+ order book before new plant is live
management quality / tone: Highly bullish, confident, and execution-focused; emphasized ‘starting line’ of growth; transparent on bottlenecks and proactive on solutions; no hedging on raw materials but pricing power demonstrated
non-obvious takeaways: D2C elevators have 58-60% gross margin — higher than industry norms due to customization and brand premium; exports priced 50% above India with no white-labeling; Ricardo’s order book is already being executed by LT — merger is administrative, not operational; 21 offices enable 400-500km coverage, making logistics feasible without heavy inventory
